metais help refusals init — Every code metais init may refuse with, and its next
step.

Next: metais init <dir>
      Writes the scaffold into a directory that is empty or does not exist yet.
  output.destination.not_directory
  output.destination.not_empty

Next: metais init <dir>
      Writes the scaffold again, into an empty directory, once the cause is
      fixed.
  output.destination.nothing_written
  output.destination.write_failed

Next: metais init --help
      Prints the operands and flags metais init takes.
  usage.bad_value
  usage.repeated_flag
  usage.unexpected_operand
  usage.unknown_flag

Next: metais init <dir> --name <name>
      Gives a name of lower-case letters, digits, single hyphens and dots, which
      the package name rule accepts.
  usage.name_invalid

Next: metais init --name <name>
      Gives the package's name, which init takes only from the command line,
      never from the working directory.
  usage.name_required
